tasks.name: rebrand-and-seo
tasks.scopedGoal: Rebrand this Next.js 16 static-export app as "OpenROAD Studio" and add production SEO/PWA metadata, while KEEPING all existing RTL→GDSII physical-design learning content, the bilingual IT/EN switcher, and the visual/lab features intact. Branding: (1) src/app/layout.tsx metadata.title should become "OpenROAD Studio — RTL → GDSII Physical Design" (or a close bilingual-neutral variant) with a matching description; (2) src/i18n/ui.ts: update siteTitle and heroBadge so the product reads as "OpenROAD Studio" in both `it` and `en` (keep the subject matter — the RTL→GDSII flow — in subtitles/descriptions); (3) src/components/Navigation.tsx header brand text should say "OpenROAD Studio"; (4) src/components/Hero.tsx: introduce "OpenROAD Studio" as the product name tastefully (e.g. in the badge or an added brand line) but DO NOT delete the RTL → GDSII headline treatment; (5) README.md title and intro; (6) package.json "name" field to "openroad-studio". Production SEO/PWA (compatible with output:"export" — read node_modules/next/dist/docs for this Next version before using metadata/route APIs): add Open Graph and Twitter card metadata to layout.tsx (or a metadata export), a robots and sitemap solution that works with static export (e.g. app/robots.ts + app/sitemap.ts if supported by this export mode, otherwise static files under public/), a web app manifest (public/manifest.webmanifest wired via metadata), and a simple SVG-based favicon/OG image referenced from metadata. Use a neutral site URL placeholder like https://openroad-studio.example (leave a comment noting it should be swapped for the real domain). Keep everything type-safe and ensure `npm run build` still produces the static export in out/.
acceptance: metadata.title and README present the product as "OpenROAD Studio"
siteTitle and heroBadge in src/i18n/ui.ts read as OpenROAD Studio in both it and en
Header (Navigation.tsx) shows the OpenROAD Studio brand
Open Graph + Twitter metadata, robots, sitemap, and a web manifest are present and wired via Next metadata
A favicon/OG image asset exists and is referenced
npm run build succeeds and emits the static export; RTL→GDSII content and IT/EN switching still work

tasks.name: code-health-ci
tasks.scopedGoal: Harden code health and add CI without touching product branding. (1) Fix all ESLint problems reported by `npm run lint` (currently 4 errors + 1 warning, all react-hooks/set-state-in-effect). The flagged locations are: src/hooks/useProgress.tsx (~line 66, setState in an empty-dep effect for localStorage hydration), src/i18n/context.tsx (~line 23, setLocaleState from a hydration effect), src/hooks/useDensity.tsx (~line 32), src/components/LearnLab.tsx (~line 276), and src/components/MobileNav.tsx. Resolve them idiomatically for React 19 — prefer lazy useState initializers guarded for SSR, useSyncExternalStore for localStorage-backed state, or event-driven updates — rather than blanket eslint-disable comments. Preserve current runtime behavior (no hydration mismatches, persisted locale/progress/density still load). (2) Ensure `npm run lint` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings and `npm run build` still succeeds. (3) Add a GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml that, on pull_request and push to main, checks out, sets up Node 20, runs `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build`. Do not modify branding files (layout.tsx, i18n/ui.ts, Navigation.tsx, Hero.tsx, README.md, package.json name).
acceptance: npm run lint reports 0 errors and 0 warnings
No blanket eslint-disable used to silence the react-hooks rule; fixes are idiomatic React 19
Persisted locale/progress/density behavior is preserved with no hydration warnings

tasks.name: merge-production
tasks.scopedGoal: Integrate the two upstream production branches into one deliverable branch and open a draft PR. The two upstream handoffs are pasted below; use the exact branch names from their `## Branch` lines. Merge both branches together on your current cloud branch (start from the rebrand-and-seo branch, then merge the code-health-ci branch into it). The two workers were scoped to disjoint files, so conflicts should be rare; if any occur, keep BOTH intents — branding/SEO changes from rebrand-and-seo and the lint/CI/hook fixes from code-health-ci — and never drop one side's work. After merging, run `npm install`, `npm run lint` (must be 0 errors, 0 warnings), and `npm run build` (must succeed). Then open a single draft PR against main titled "OpenROAD Studio production" summarizing the rebrand, SEO/PWA additions, code-health fixes, and CI. Do not rewrite history of the source branches.
